name: intelligent_support_pipeline
title: Zendesk Intelligent Support Pipeline
description:
A 7-step governed Support-Ops pipeline built entirely on the jayy/zendesk-integration module's orchestration commands. Every step mints a signed receipt visible in Studio's Receipts tab; the workflow-level receipt merkle-roots the seven node receipts.

Triggered by a webhook, the workflow: (1) provisions the requester as a Zendesk user, (2) opens a governed support ticket via the airlock, (3) auto-detects the requester's company from their email domain and links the ticket to the matching organization (creating it if missing), (4) deduplicates any open tickets from the same requester and merges them, (5) applies a welcome macro — but ONLY if no duplicates were found (preventing double-responses on merged tickets), (6) compiles a daily support digest report with ticket counts by status and priority, and (7) posts the full digest to Slack via a direct webhook POST.

Orchestration composites used: auto_assign_organization (domain-to-org matching), merge_duplicate_tickets (dedup engine), apply_macro_to_ticket (conditional template application), generate_support_digest (metrics rollup). Each composite wraps 2-5 API calls behind a single airlock approval.

Trigger contract: POST a JSON body with fields: name (string), email (valid email), subject (string), message (string), macro_id (integer — your welcome macro ID from zendesk.list_macros), slack_channel_webhook (string — your Slack Incoming Webhook URL from api.slack.com/apps).

Dependencies: Requires jayy/zendesk-integration v1.3.0 or later. No Slack module required — Slack notification is a direct HTTP POST to your Incoming Webhook URL.

Why apply the macro AFTER deduplication: If the requester already has open tickets (i.e. duplicates were merged), firing the welcome macro again would send a second welcome reply on a ticket that is already being handled. The conditional guard (merged_count == 0) ensures the macro only fires for genuinely new requesters. [contest:2026Q3]
